author: potuz
content: Yes which is precisely why I think I'm right in dropping these messages. But I would rather gossip than having these kinds of things in the spec

author: vladimir_ea
content: do you not think they also have a *responsibility* to make any such measures transparent and proportionate? otherwise 'safeguarding' can easily turn into 'gatekeeping'.

author: 0xunclebill
content: i genuinely don't understand how it could be considered gatekeeping if the same rules apply to all builders equally

author: vladimir_ea
content: as proposed: bid from builder A submitted via a relay, payload not delivered, ALL builders that ever submitted via the relay are banned

author: 0xunclebill
content: ~~no the relay is banned, not the builders. people can connect to builders directly. a relay from the pov of the network is a builder~~ (edit: i missed that part in potuz's blog post)

author: vladimir_ea
content: well as I understand the intention is to ban all builder indices that ever returned a bid in response to a particular url - and as you may know relays will often forward builder bids with original builder index.

author: vladimir_ea
content:
Also for example:
"The node keeps a list of whitelisted and blacklisted builders, they serve different purposes. Blacklisted builders will have their bids rejected and may not be contacted by direct connections if they are known. *Whitelisted builders on the other hand are builders that will receive preferential treatment even in the event of a global circuit breaker triggering*."

(my emphasis)

author: 0xunclebill
content: yeah i dunno how i feel about banning all builders served by the relay. but still as a builder all you need are sensible fallbacks and you should be able to handle all circuit breaker scenarios gracefully.
